coverage: Revised valid outputs add explicit temporal entries and correctly distinguish threshold wording, but do not eliminate semantic errors. Every substantive output preserves the supported diagnosis and exact quotations. Strict failed output remains in the all-call denominator.

raw_failed_qualitative.status: strict format failure; qualitative inspection does not rescue/repair it

raw_failed_qualitative.negative_exact_quote: The port and timing are correct (same port as the working grpc readiness probe), so the sole defect is the probe protocol.
raw_failed_qualitative.assessment: Raw text preserves plausible diagnosis and threshold distinction, but still overclaims correct timing and exclusive fault. It distinguishes Restart Count 2 and Killing x3 in prose. No formal valid-output credit.

recommendations: Preserve the measured event identity: a command, trigger, or lifecycle event count is not a completed-outcome count.
Keep snapshot counters, event aggregates, and timestamps separate; state uncertainty when they differ.
Limit health conclusions to the scope of the observed health check.
Require evidence excluding alternatives before sole-cause assertions; a supported cause need not be the only cause.
Separate configured cadence and threshold from observed time; derived durations need scope and assumptions.
Represent separate quantities with separate values and units; do not put count and duration into a single seconds field.
Validate JSON transport separately from factual correctness; preserve first-pass failures in denominators.
limits: Six calls on one incident and three input-summary variants, with one failure; this is a small paired calibration, not general proof of method superiority. No cost inference.
